subject: Pricing follow-up: startup program + committed-use options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Miller <evan@deepfin.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: startup program + committed-use options

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really enjoyed the deep dive on DeepFin's ingestion pipeline and where inference gets called out in the stack. Quick recap and a few questions so we can pull together a concrete term sheet:  

Recap (as I have it):
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + entity extraction for financial docs (models: open-gen variants).
- Current pilot estimate: ~50M tokens/month (generation + embeddings combined).
- Ramp plan: 50M -> 150M by month 3, target ~300M tokens/month by month 12.
- Target SLA: <300ms p95 for short-turn queries, batching acceptable for background jobs.

Pricing / budget notes from call:
- You mentioned a target spend in the $8k–$25k/mo range as you validate latency/usability tradeoffs.
- You asked about a target $/1M tokens we could hit with committed terms.

Questions for you so we can model unit economics properly:
1) Can you confirm expected steady-state tokens/mo at month 6 and month 12? (I currently have 150M @ M6, 300M @ M12)
2) Is there a target $/1M tokens you need us to model for internal approval? (you said you were hoping for a sub-$500/1M figure — is that right?)
3) Any constraints on PO timing / contracting cadence for a 12mo vs 24mo commit?

Next steps I propose:
- If the numbers above look right, I can share: (a) Redwood startup program term summary (one-page) and (b) a committed-use term sheet with tiered discounts by monthly token commitment.
- Marissa and I will model a couple of pricing scenarios (startup + committed-use stacking) and send a recommended starter offer for DeepFin.

Attachments: I’ll attach the Redwood_Startup_Tier_Terms.pdf and a sample committed-use term sheet once we finalize the numbers — sending after you confirm the M6/M12 volumes.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

---
From: Evan Miller <evan@deepfin.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@deepfin.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: startup program + committed-use options

Ben — thanks, this lines up with our notes. Confirming:
- M6 expected steady-state: 150M tokens/month.
- M12 target: 300M tokens/month.
- Target budget: initial pilot ~ $10k/mo, scaling to $20k–$25k/mo by M6–M12 as we move into production.
- Target unit: we're hoping to land around $400–$500 per 1M tokens for production workloads, but we need to see a committed-use proposal to present to finance.

A few asks:
1) Please include any startup program credits / % off in year 1 and how that stacks with committed-use discounts.
2) We are interested in seeing 12mo vs 24mo pricing (and any multi-year incentive for a 2yr commit).
3) Can you send a short term sheet / pricing spreadsheet we can circulate internally?

If you can get those docs over by EOD Wednesday PT that would be great — we have a finance review next week.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Product, DeepFin
evan@deepfin.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing follow-up: startup program + committed-use options

Marissa / Aditya — looping you both in. Evan confirmed M6=150M / M12=300M and is looking for a $400–$500 per 1M target with startup credits + committed-use options. Finance review next week.

My ask: can you advise on recommended public discount bands we can offer for this profile? Thoughts:
- Startup program: 6–12 months of credits or % off for seed-stage / pre-revenue — historically we've done 40% off for qualifying startups on year 1 list pricing.
- Committed-use: for ~300M tokens/month steady-state (annualized ~3.6B tokens), what's a reasonable tiered offer? e.g., 12mo commit at $100k ARR-ish gives X% off, 24mo commit gives an additional Y% or invoice timing advantage.

Specific proposal I'm thinking of to test with DeepFin:
A) Starter: Startup program (if eligible) = 40% off list for 12 months + $20k credit applied to first invoice.
B) Committed use: 12mo commit at 2.5B tokens/year (averaged tier) => 25% committed discount on top of startup credit for year 1; 24mo commit => 30% + 5% multi-year incentive (applied as price hold / true-up).

Can you both sanity-check the arithmetic and let me know if we should flag any approvals required (legal / revenue ops / revrec)? If you can return a clean term sheet I can send Evan by EOD Wed.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Proposal looks good directionally. A few confirmations before we sign off:
- DeepFin is seed-stage with YC alumni; we should qualify for the startup program. Please include the eligibility checklist in the one-pager.
- We prefer a 12mo commit to start, with the option to extend to 24mo after Q2 review.
- If you can hit an effective ~$450/1M tokens in year 1 (after startup stacking + committed discount), we can get an internal nod and cut a PO.

I'm attaching the PO draft (DeepFin_PO_20260623.pdf) — this is contingent on a term sheet with the numbers we agreed. Once we have the term sheet we can route to legal and finance. Also happy to take a DocuSign link if that speeds things up.

Thanks —
Evan
Head of Product, DeepFin
